what: A finding retired by any edit to its file could never be re-reported: the retired row held the fingerprint and the re-report was skipped.
how: On a fingerprint hit whose stored state is retired (and the file digest is known), file the re-report as a new open row under fid + '#' + digest instead of skipping. A new key rather than flipping the old row, because _merge_ledgers ranks retired above open and a stale co-writer would win a flipped row back.

what: --check returned 0 when every scale was unscored, so allsweep graded a measurement of nothing as clean.
how: Return 1 (with a stderr line) when the number of unscored rows is not below the number of rows, i.e. nothing produced a rho. Live data (1 of 8 scored) keeps rc 0.

what: A TIERS.json re-chart crossing a power of two changed widths and silently re-addressed every published world on the next hand-run.
how: New moved_addresses(path, addrs) compares against the standing SHELFMARKS.json; main() refuses (rc 1, file untouched) if any published designation's address would change, unless --readdress is passed. An unparseable standing file also refuses. Verified 0 moved against all 1,016 live addresses, so today's run is unaffected.

what: The bidirectional substring section bind let the roll name DC bind to Sword Coast Adventurer's Guide.
how: New SUBSTRING_MIN_NORM = 8: the substring arm needs the shorter normalised side to be at least 8 characters (exact match unchanged, any length). Every legitimate live non-exact bind has 9+ (shortest 'sexworker'). Not done: refusing a title already bound to another roll row.

what: Bare \b(401|402)\b in permanent_refusal read a token count or retry-after as a dead key and benched a live bucket for four hours.
how: _PERMANENT_CODES now needs the code introduced as a status (http/status/code/error/returned/... before it), followed by a status phrase (401 Unauthorized), or opening the string. All drill wordings (HTTP 401 invalid api key, HTTP 402 payment required, HTTP 401 Authentication error) still match; 'Requested 401' and 'retry after 401' no longer do.

what: _extract_json returned the first complete inner object of a cut-off reply.
how: When raw_decode fails because the text ran out (JSONDecodeError message starts 'Unterminated', or error position at end of text) return None instead of scanning inward. A stray '{' in prose fails early and still moves to the next brace; prose-then-JSON and fenced JSON still parse.

what: --refine could overwrite ROSETTA.json with {} when the records/hosts join matched nothing.
how: Refuse (rc 1, nothing written) when the mine is non-empty and refine keeps zero rows. A zero-survivor floor rather than a fractional one: a first refine from the raw mine legitimately drops about 90% of rows (raw 139 KB vs standing 7 KB), so a MINE_FLOOR-style ratio would block the normal case. A partial-but-nonzero short join is not caught; see notes.

what: A record file with entries: null crashed the whole resync with TypeError.
how: A record whose entries is present but not a list is folded into unreadable (noted and counted) like the other malformed shapes. The second half (two record files declaring one source, alphabetically last wins) is not changed; it is reported to the operator and no live duplicates exist, see Q7.

what: Input-size refusals and capped calls with no finish_reason are recorded but never benched, so the same bucket is re-claimed each call.
how: Options: (a) N consecutive of either earns a bench like UNPARSEABLE_STRIKES_BEFORE_BENCH; (b) leave, on the view that a size refusal is per-request not per-bucket. It is a routing-policy choice on the load-bearing router, not a defect fix.

what: On a failover success _clear(pinned.bucket) resets the pinned bucket's deadline strikes.
how: Options: clear only the bucket that actually served (needs the served bucket from the engine result), or keep as is so a bucket that alternates misses and failovers stays at the first 60 s bench. Changes escalation behaviour of the router; owner call.

what: The sroffset follow in scales_for had no iteration bound, so a repeating continue would spin one query for ever.
how: Track offsets already requested per query and stop when one repeats. No page cap (Hard Rule 0), so a genuinely long result set is still read to its end.

what: dead_forever() returns an empty set once POOL_PROOF.json is over an hour old, so every permanent exclusion not in OWNER_EXCLUDED lapses if the prover stops.
how: Options: keep the fail-open (a stale proof is not evidence, and a lapse costs a re-probe not a wrong answer), or fail closed by keeping the last known dead set past PROOF_TTL. The TTL is documented as deliberate; which side an aged proof errs to is an owner ruling.

what: repass_bands, via pipeline.records(), never sees a record with empty entries, so an unearned source-level provisional_magnitude on a purged record is never demoted.
how: Fix would be in pipeline.records() (not mine, and other callers rely on it skipping empties) or a separate all-records reader in repass_bands. Options: add a reader here that includes empty-entry records for the demotion pass only, or accept that a purged record's synthesis is out of scope.

what: address_space.main and pantheon.main write derived state with no escalation.assert_clear halt interlock (carried from b07 Q4).
how: Options: add assert_clear on the write path of both (consistent with corpus writers, drill's hand-run roster would then need both listed), or leave them as derived-state writers that are regenerable. Owner's call between the two classes; note F3's refusal now reduces the harm of the address_space case.

what: Two record files declaring the same source: the alphabetically last wins regardless of entry count, so a stub sorting last would set the roll to the stub's count.
how: Options: prefer the file with more entries, refuse to resync that source and report it, or leave as is (already listed in the output, no live duplicates). Picking a winner by size can pick a purged-then-restored file wrongly, so it is a curatorial choice.
